slots.title: Trump still weighing diesel export ban
slots.body:
Reuters reported Trump said he still considers a diesel export ban and talks about it “every day” as the White House focuses on energy prices.

CNBC quoted him as still “thinking about” the ban while flagging a possible “negative impact” on gasoline.

Brent crude settled at 96.99, down 1.1% on the session; the U.S. oil fund $USO was up 1.6% to 145.66 in the cross-asset snapshot.

No ban was announced in the coverage—only that the option remains on the table.

Which energy price do you track when policy headlines hit—diesel at the pump or crude on the screen?

slots.title: US session recap — Oct. 1, 2026
slots.body:
The S&P 500 settled at 7,651.54, down 0.3% (-19.30), after an intraday high of 7,722.88.
The index did not hold the morning-side of the range into the close.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 443.87 points, closing at 50,906.05 (-0.9%).
That was the weakest major US benchmark in the set, with a session low matching the final print at 50,906.05.

The Nasdaq Composite finished at 26,861.06, up 0.2% (+63.52), so tech-heavy exposure ended slightly green even as the broad large-cap index slipped.

The Russell 2000 closed at 2,796.86, down 0.4% (-11.06), a modest small-cap decline in line with the S&P’s direction.

The VIX rose to 16.34, up 1.9% (+0.30), with an intraday band of 15.62 to 16.61.

Sector averages on Nasdaq for the date showed Consumer Cyclical up 0.7%, the only clear positive among the eleven groups.
Financial Services led declines at -2.0%, Utilities at -2.2%, Consumer Defensive at -1.8%, Energy at -1.1%, and Real Estate at -1.2%.
Technology averaged -0.1%, essentially flat.

Megacap tech was mixed.
Apple closed at 333.02 (+1.1%), Amazon at 249.15 (+1.0%), Microsoft at 512.90 (+0.8%), and Alphabet Class A at 344.08 (+0.9%).
Meta Platforms fell to 725.18 (-1.8%).
NVIDIA finished at 228.38 (+0.5%).
Tesla closed at 354.81 (+0.6%).

Financial and healthcare heavyweights weighed on the Dow tape: UnitedHealth at 367.08 (-2.1%), Bank of America at 54.43 (-1.0%), and Johnson & Johnson at 264.74 (-1.1%).
Broadcom closed at 351.19 (-1.1%).

Several names on the earnings calendar for 2026-10-01 moved sharply by the close.
McCormick Class A ($MKC) finished at 46.40 (-4.1%).
McCormick Class V ($MKC-V) at 47.94 (-4.2%).
Nike ($NKE) at 35.40 (-1.2%), with a session low of 35.16 against a 52-week low of 35.16 in the profile data.
Acuity Brands ($AYI) closed at 310.71 (+0.6%).

Intel was among the most active liquid names, up 3.7% to 120.23.
Overseas, Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 2.7% to 68,556.69 in the injected overseas set.

Treasury snapshot dated 2026-09-29 in the data showed the 10-year at 5.3% and the 2s10s spread at 0.37.
Gold futures (GCUSD) settled at 4,205.10 (+0.4%).
The US Oil Fund (USO proxy in cross_asset) closed at 145.66 (+1.6%), while Brent crude (BZUSD) was at 96.98 (-1.1%).
The dollar fund proxy UUP finished at 28.77 (+0.1%).
Bitcoin (BTCUSD) was at 83,748.20 (+0.2%).

The economic calendar in the feed scheduled US initial jobless claims, continuing claims, and September ISM manufacturing readings for 2026-10-01; the injected bundle did not include released actuals for those prints.
